info.title: Skins.com Trading API
info.description:
The Skins.com trading API lets bots and apps trade CS2 items: list items from your Steam inventory, reprice and cancel listings, buy fixed-price items, bid on auctions, and follow every change live on the websocket.

**Money fields are integer USD cents.** `coin_value`, `market_value`, `bid_value` and the other money fields are in cents: 100 means $1.00.

Authentication: create a key under Profile > Developers (two-factor authentication is required to create one) and send `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

Rate limits: 120 requests per 60 seconds per IP across all endpoints. Going over locks the IP out for 60 seconds with HTTP 429. Buying, selling and bidding also have per-account limits. Prefer the websocket to polling.

Pricing: a listing price can be edited once every 5 minutes. Bids must be at least the next bid (`purchase_price`) and are placed at exactly the next bid.

Websocket: socket.io v4 at `wss://trading-api.skins.com`, path `/s/`, namespace `/trade`. Get `socket_token` and `socket_signature` from `GET /metadata/socket`, connect with query `uid` and `token`, then emit `identify` `{ uid, model, authorizationToken, signature }` if `init.authenticated` is false. Emit `filters` to start receiving item events, and optionally `allowedEvents` `{ events: [...] }` to limit them. Every item event payload is an array. Events are listed under `x-websocket-events`.

MCP: AI agents can use the API through the MCP server at `https://trading-api.skins.com/mcp` (Streamable HTTP). Every endpoint is a tool named after its operation id, with `-` replaced by `_` (`create-deposit` is `create_deposit`). Send the same `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header; tool calls count against the same rate limits.

get.description: Returns the user object and the socket credentials (`socket_token`, `socket_signature`) used to authenticate on the websocket. The token is valid for 30 seconds.

get.description: Your tradable CS2 inventory. `id` is the Steam asset id; use it (or `asset_id`) to deposit. Items already in a deposit carry an `invalid` reason, except deposits back on the market after an auction ended unsold: those can be deposited again to re-auction them.

parameters.name: invalid
parameters.description: "yes" filters out items that cannot be deposited

401.description: Missing, invalid or revoked API key

429.description: Rate limited: 120 requests per 60 s per IP, then locked out for 60 s

post.description: List items for sale. `coin_value` is the price in USD cents. Send at most 20 items per request. Each item gets a tracking code; the listing result arrives as `new_item` or `deposit_failed` on the websocket. Depositing an item whose auction ended unsold replaces its old deposit with a new one (new deposit id): the old one arrives as `deleted_item`, the new one as `new_item`.

coin_value.description: Highest price you accept (USD cents); defaults to the current price

bid_value.description: Bid (USD cents); must be at least the next bid

updated_item.description: Items whose price or state changed.

deleted_item.description: Deposit ids that are no longer available.

trade_status.description: Status changes of your trades. `type` is `deposit` for your sales and `withdrawal` for your purchases.

init.description: Sent on connect and after `identify`. `authenticated` tells whether the socket is signed in.

timesync.description: Server time in milliseconds, sent in reply to a `timesync` emit.

identify.description: Authenticate the socket with the credentials from `GET /metadata/socket`.

filters.description: Start receiving item events. Optional `price_min` / `price_max` (USD cents) and `auction` ("yes") narrow them.

allowedEvents.description: Limit which events this socket receives.
